question: Why were California home claims so much higher in the first half of 2026 than a year earlier?

report.interpretation: California home claims counted by loss date, Jan–Jun 2026 versus Jan–Jun 2025, using claim count, claim frequency (claims per 1,000 policy-months), severity (incurred per claim, paid plus reserve) and loss ratio. The latest months aren't in the comparison, so late reporting doesn't affect it.
report.answer: The increase is real: 122 claims in H1 2026 against 79 in H1 2025, up 54%. It comes from a bigger book, not riskier policies. Home policy-months in California rose from about 17,900 to 27,500 (+54%). The cause is a large batch of partner-channel policies that started in January 2026, about 530 a month in total across LA, San Diego and the Bay Area. Claim frequency was flat at 4.41 against 4.43 per 1,000 policy-months. Partner policies produced 40 of the 122 claims. Claims from all other channels were 82, almost the same as the 79 a year earlier. There was no California weather event in the weather table. Cost per claim also rose, from about $11.8k to $15.4k, and the loss ratio went from 0.40 to 0.53. That rise is not from the partner book. Partner claims average about $11.0k, while the non-partner claims average about $17.6k, up from $11.8k. The non-partner rise is concentrated in a few large water_damage and wind_hail claims in LA and San Diego, and it is a small sample, so I can't say whether it is more than noise.
report.answer_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT CASE WHEN month>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, sum(policies_in_force) pm, sum(earned_premium) ep FROM exposure_monthly WHERE region='California' AND product='home' AND (month BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-01' OR month BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-01') GROUP BY 1), c AS (SELECT CASE WHEN loss_date>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, count(*) n, sum(coalesce(pay.paid,0)+reserve_amount) inc FROM claims c LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE region='California' AND product='home' AND (loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' OR loss_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30') GROUP BY 1) SELECT h, n, round(pm) policy_months, round(1000*n/pm,2) freq_per_1000_pm, round(inc/n) severity, round(inc/ep,3) loss_ratio FROM c JOIN e USING(h) ORDER BY h

findings.claim: Claim count rose 54% while exposure rose by about the same amount, so frequency was flat. Severity and loss ratio increased.
findings.evidence_sql: WITH e AS (SELECT CASE WHEN month>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, sum(policies_in_force) pm, sum(earned_premium) ep FROM exposure_monthly WHERE region='California' AND product='home' AND (month BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-01' OR month BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-01') GROUP BY 1), c AS (SELECT CASE WHEN loss_date>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, count(*) n, sum(coalesce(pay.paid,0)+reserve_amount) inc FROM claims c LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE region='California' AND product='home' AND (loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' OR loss_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30') GROUP BY 1) SELECT h, n, round(pm) policy_months, round(1000*n/pm,2) freq_per_1000_pm, round(inc/n) severity, round(inc/ep,3) loss_ratio FROM c JOIN e USING(h) ORDER BY h

findings.claim: Partner-channel policies began in January 2026, about 530 new a month. Claims from other channels were flat, and partner claims have lower severity.
findings.evidence_sql: SELECT h, ch, n, sev FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN c.loss_date>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, CASE WHEN p.channel='partner' THEN 'partner' ELSE 'other' END ch, count(*) n, round(avg(coalesce(pay.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount)) sev FROM claims c JOIN policies p USING(policy_id) LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE c.region='California' AND c.product='home' AND (c.loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' OR c.loss_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30') GROUP BY ALL) ORDER BY 1,2

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mix of business change: a new partner-channel book
hypotheses.evidence: Partner policies went from none to about 530 new a month from January 2026. Exposure and claims grew about 54%, and frequency didn't change.
The weather_events table has no California events.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Data problem such as duplicated rows or an incomplete period
hypotheses.evidence: There are no duplicate claim rows, and the compared periods (Jan–Jun) are old enough to be complete.
Non-partner severity rose from $11.8k to $17.6k, driven by a few large water_damage and wind_hail claims. The sample is small, so noise can't be ruled out.

data_quality_issues.issue: There are 15 extreme reserve_amount outliers across the warehouse, up to $178k.
data_quality_issues.impact: A few large reserves can move severity and loss ratio in a small segment like California home.

WITH source AS (
    SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
           coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
           c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
    FROM claims c
    JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
    LEFT JOIN (
        SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id

FROM source

  AND region IN ('California')

GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL

content.thinking: There's a partner channel launching January 2026, bringing around 540 policies per month. Frequency looks flat, but severity jumped from 11.8k to 15.4k, pushing the loss ratio from 0.40 to 0.53 — I want to check severity broken down by channel to understand this better, so I'll run a quick query on claims by channel and severity.

input.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN c.loss_date>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, CASE WHEN p.channel='partner' THEN 'partner' ELSE 'other' END ch, count(*) n, round(avg(coalesce(pay.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount)) sev FROM claims c JOIN policies p USING(policy_id) LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE c.region='California' AND c.product='home' AND (c.loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' OR c.loss_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

content.thinking: Non-partner claims stayed roughly flat while partner claims added 40, and the severity of other claims jumped from 11.8k to 17.6k, likely driven by a few large wind/hail or water losses in SD rather than a broad trend. That seems sufficient to work with.

input.sql: SELECT h, ch, n, sev FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN c.loss_date>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, CASE WHEN p.channel='partner' THEN 'partner' ELSE 'other' END ch, count(*) n, round(avg(coalesce(pay.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount)) sev FROM claims c JOIN policies p USING(policy_id) LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE c.region='California' AND c.product='home' AND (c.loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' OR c.loss_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30') GROUP BY ALL) ORDER BY 1,2

WITH e AS (SELECT CASE WHEN month>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, sum(policies_in_force) pm, sum(earned_premium) ep FROM exposure_monthly WHERE region='California' AND product='home' AND (month BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-01' OR month BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-01') GROUP BY 1), c AS (SELECT CASE WHEN loss_date>='2026-01-01' THEN '2026H1' ELSE '2025H1' END h, count(*) n, sum(coalesce(pay.paid,0)+reserve_amount) inc FROM claims c LEFT JOIN (SELECT claim_id,sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1) pay USING(claim_id) WHERE region='California' AND product='home' AND (loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-06-30' OR loss_date BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30') GROUP BY 1) SELECT h, n, round(pm) policy_months, round(1000*n/pm,2) freq_per_1000_pm, round(inc/n) severity, round(inc/ep,3) loss_ratio FROM c JOIN e USING(h) ORDER BY h
